conversation.output: Found 14 references in sessionWorkspaces.ts, EditorPanel.svelte, and editorStore.svelte.ts.

conversation.text: The editor belongs to the session workspace. Switching hides the pane and retains its view state; removal is the explicit disposal boundary.
Check whether the transcript follows the same ownership rule.
It does not. Transcript rows are derived from stored conversation items and virtualized by turn, while the terminal projection has its own attach and release lifecycle.
Show the evidence for the virtualization boundary.
rg -n "createVirtualizer|turn-row" ConversationTimeline.svelte
ConversationTimeline groups items into turns, gives each turn one measured virtual row, and keeps six rows of overscan. Long replies are measured after paint rather than assigned a fixed height.
Does opening an older conversation jump to the newest message?
Only when there is no saved scroll position. A previously read conversation restores its recorded scroll top after the rows mount.
Inspect the compact file tree row.
The row is 28 pixels tall, indents by 12 pixels per level, keeps ignored files visible but muted, and shows child counts only for directories.
What information is visible in source control?
Each row leads with a status letter, then the file name and folder. Mixed staged and unstaged state remains visible as a short qualifier.
Keep actions disabled in this fixture.
The source-control rows have no repository root and are read-only. Their presentation is real, but no repository operation can run.
How should agent activity read at a glance?
Status, task, and known message count fit into two lines. Working, done, failed, and idle remain distinct without inventing information that is not available.
Confirm the editor is a real CodeMirror surface.
The fixture mounts CodeMirrorSourceEditor in read-only mode with a static TypeScript document and the same language and theme extensions as the workbench.
Check the empty-state path without changing this populated scenario.
The timeline still accepts an empty label, but this route intentionally exercises the populated state so row density and scrolling remain inspectable.
Why are completed work details folded?
Finished commands and tool output collapse under a Worked line so the conversation reads as prompts and answers first. The details remain one click away.
Keep enough rows here to exercise windowing.
This static transcript continues well beyond the visible frame. Scrolling mounts measured turns around the viewport instead of rendering the whole history at once.
Does the fixture write scroll position anywhere?
No. The route passes a fixed initial scroll position and no persistence callback. Reloading reconstructs everything from the JSON payload.
Does it request older messages?
No. The transcript is complete in the fixture, hasOlder is false, and no history loader is supplied.
Keep this page unavailable in production.
The route load guard checks both SvelteKit’s development flag and Vite’s DEV flag, then returns a 404 outside development.
Use the existing Assembly colors.
The page imports the /next token and utility styles, then frames each real surface with those existing surface, border, text, and accent tokens.
Avoid redesigning the underlying rows.
The fixture supplies only a panel shell and headings. File, change, agent, conversation, and editor rendering stays owned by the production presentation components.
Can I inspect selected row states?
Yes. File and agent rows update an in-memory selection on click, and directory rows can be expanded or collapsed without touching application stores.
Include nested file paths and ignored content.
The tree includes nested shell panels, route files, an ignored build directory, and a mix of TypeScript, Svelte, CSS, JSON, and Markdown icons.
Include mixed Git states.
The source-control list covers modified, added, deleted, renamed, untracked, staged, and mixed index/worktree examples.
Include all agent status tones.
Working, done, failed, and idle rows are present, including both known and unknown message counts.
Make the source document substantial enough to scroll.
The TypeScript fixture contains typed records, derived status labels, filtering, grouping, and a sample export. It is long enough to exercise gutters and editor scrolling.
Does the fixture call the network?
No. Every displayed record and document line is imported from the local JSON file, and the page supplies no fetch path.
Does it depend on Tauri?
No. Actions that could reach native services are disabled or receive inert callbacks, so the route is safe in the Vite browser preview.
Add stable inspection anchors.
The page and each of its five component surfaces carry explicit data-testid anchors.
Keep the layout useful at narrower widths.
The secondary panels collapse from three columns to one while preserving fixed inspection heights for virtualization and CodeMirror.
Do not add a scenario framework.
There is one populated Assembly scenario and no registry, switcher, query parameter, or persistence layer.
What should a reviewer verify first?
Open the route in development, confirm all five surfaces are populated, then scroll the conversation and editor and click a file and agent row.
Keep the fixture deterministic.
IDs, timestamps, statuses, paths, counts, and source content are fixed in JSON. No clock or random value participates in rendering.
Summarize the fixture boundary.
A development-only route renders real Assembly presentation components against one static JSON document. It owns no application state and performs no external work.
